title: the Glass Steppe Rising Again
premise: Wren Brightwater, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, keeps the ledgers of the Glass Steppe guild, which trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names not yet earned. When a dying stranger presses a map into her hands, she discovers it charts the path to a king who has been slowly replaced by the thing wearing his crown, sustained by the last living dragon-fire. Pursued by crown wardens and haunted by the oaths of dead swordspeakers, Wren must decide whether justice can exist outside the law she once served. In the end, she unbinds the king by speaking her final oath, spending her own memories of belonging to feed the guttering dragon-fire—and wakes in a guild that remembers her ledgers but not her face, free at last and belonging to no one.
about_author: L. M. Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing broken legal documents before turning to fantasy. They write about people who keep records of things the world would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. In the guildhall on the Glass Steppe, Wren audits a shipment of bottled thunder and argues with her mentor about an oath she swore as a child. A stranger collapses at the door, dying of wounds no blade made, and presses a scorched map into her hands with a whispered warning: 'The king is already gone.' Emotional beat: reluctant duty—the moment refusing becomes impossible.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Wren, alternating with the thing wearing the crown. Following the map across salt flats, Wren evades crown wardens and learns from a disgraced court physician that the king's mind was traded away piece by piece for peace treaties. The crown-thing senses her coming through the dragon-fire's fading light. Emotional beat: dread deepening into resolve as she realizes the law itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire, Guttering
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Beneath the palace, Wren finds the last dragon chained to the throne's foundations, its fire feeding the crown-thing's stolen shape, and the true king—a hollowed man who begs her not to save him. Wardens corner her; her swordspeaker oaths rise unbidden, and she cuts them down outside any law. Emotional beat: climax—grief and fury fused into the choice that will cost her everything.

chapters.title: An Oath Spoken Once
chapters.summary: POV: Wren, then the guild in her absence. Wren speaks her final oath, pouring her memories of home and belonging into the dragon-fire; it blazes free, burning the crown-thing away and leaving the king mortal, accountable, and alive to face judgment. The freed dragon carries her back to the Steppe before dissolving into dawn. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—justice paid for with memory, and a strange new freedom in being forgotten.
